purpose: Screen two additional San Agustin Table 1 fish labels against current taxonomy and Philippine voucher or freshwater-range evidence.

method.scope: Focused review of Lutjanus johnii and Microphis brachyurus, two printed labels in Table 1 of the 2025 San Agustin article.
method.distinction: Philippine market vouchers, North Luzon barcodes, and national freshwater checklist entries provide range or identification context only. They do not identify the preserved San Agustin survey specimens or assign them to any waterbody or reach.
method.evidenceLimit: The North Luzon barcode paper's main table lists accession numbers but says per-sample collection detail is in supplementary tables; the sample-level source locality was not resolved here. The San Agustin paper still has no voucher accession crosswalk, diagnostic images, meristic data, sequences, coordinates, or individual reach-to-specimen link.
method.sourceReuse: Only concise attributed findings and direct source links are retained. No specimen image, market dataset, occurrence export, supplementary workbook, sequence, coordinate, or transformed app row was copied. Public-app reuse approval was not assessed or granted.

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank match (usage key 2384936; confidence 99). This nomenclatural match does not identify the San Agustin specimen.
findings.currentAuthority: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes treats Lutjanus johnii (Bloch, 1792) as valid and gives an Indo-West Pacific range extending east to the Philippines and Fiji; it lists brackish and marine habitat. The Panay fish guide describes juveniles in brackish waters and illustrates a UPVMI 1512 voucher (169.9 mm SL).
findings.philippineContext: A 2025 North Luzon DNA-barcode paper includes Lutjanus johnii accessions COI PP460037 and 12S PP554435 in a voucher-linked dataset of 1,513 samples gathered from markets, landing sites, and rivers. The article directs sample-level locality details to supplementary tables; the source locality of this species' voucher was not extracted here. Separately, Smithsonian NMNH USNM 423648 (field label PHI-234) is cataloged as L. johnii from a 2013 Philippines market survey, with a Tacloban City Market locality string; FDA's reference library links PHI-234 to COI accession OQ387612. These are identification and market-provenance records, not capture-point evidence.
findings.disposition: The accepted name, Philippine market vouchers, and Panay guide make the label nationally plausible in coastal/brackish context. None confirms the survey specimen or its San Agustin reach. No new range-authority discrepancy or voucher-priority mismatch is added.
findings.priority: routine; compare the RSU voucher with diagnostic characters for L. johnii and retain a specimen-to-sequence link before assigning a reach

findings.nameCrosswalk: The existing strict GBIF Backbone crosswalk returned an exact accepted species-rank match (usage key 5712324; confidence 99). This nomenclatural match does not identify the San Agustin specimen.
findings.currentAuthority: Jamandre's 2023 provisional freshwater-fish checklist treats Microphis brachyurus as native in Philippine river basins and cites Philippine material including voucher USNM 102599. WoRMS and the 2023 integrative revision use M. brachyurus as an accepted name. A 2025 phylogeographic study analyzed 91 COI sequences and found West- and Central-Pacific population groups while retaining one nominal M. brachyurus; its sampled localities do not provide a San Agustin or Philippine voucher identification.
findings.philippineContext: The North Luzon DNA-barcode paper also lists M. brachyurus accessions COI PP422986-PP422987 and 12S PP515699 in its voucher-linked dataset, but its main table does not identify this voucher's individual collection site. FishBase attributes reports from Calbiga-a Creek, Lagu Lagu Creek, and Ambacan River at Baybay, Leyte to Kottelat's 1993 technical report; only the bibliographic record and a compiled summary were retrieved, not the full report. Treat those as a historical source lead, not a rechecked specimen record.
findings.disposition: The national checklist and historical freshwater-report lead support Philippine river-basin plausibility, but do not establish MIMAROPA presence or identify the San Agustin specimen. The 2025 population-structure study is a reason to retain specimen-level sequence context, not a basis for splitting the survey name. No new range-authority discrepancy or voucher-priority mismatch is added.
findings.priority: routine; request the RSU voucher, locality/station mapping, and any linked sequence before asserting a local river or estuary record

nextAction: Continue the current-authority and range screen for the remaining 9 of 39 Table 1 labels. Keep six voucher-priority mismatch labels in the verification queue and retain four separate range-authority discrepancies: Tridentiger trigonocephalus, Hypseleotris cyprinoides, Eleotris mauritiana, and Awaous guamensis. Then seek the RSU voucher/accession crosswalk and resolve the paper's station/locality conflicts before considering occurrence rows.
